name: 3D Motion Graphics
visualIdentity: A broad 3D direction, not tied to photorealism or one engine. Choose photorealistic, cartoon, or stylized rendering; use coherent geometry, bevels, roughness, reflections, contact shadows, clear key lighting, and deliberate perspective or orthographic framing.
suitableUses: Hero object renders, product launches, brand stings, feature breakdowns, explanatory scenes, and interactive campaign pieces when real depth or material detail helps tell the story. These are inferred fits; style is flexible across subjects and media.
limitations: Avoid intersections, floating objects, inconsistent scale, and blown highlights. Use simulation only when it adds value; XPBD needs a suitable verified solver and does not inherently provide fluids, plasticity, tearing, or origami. Preserve label legibility and avoid unsupported scientific implications. A flat image cannot support a true camera dolly or orbit.
palette: No canonical palette is specified. Example fallback tokens are background #EDE9E1, foreground #303C40, accent #748E8A, and accent #B9866C; they are reference dependent, not style requirements. Supplied, brand, and source colors take precedence; preserve roles and asset colors. Use discrete colors, no proposed gradient. Accent/foreground contrast is below the 4.5 text target; verify actual compositing and place text on a suitable existing backing.
motionAndInteraction: Use weighted rotation, assembly, and camera movement with clear contact and readable holds. Make video state deterministic and seekable; bake or replay simulations from fixed state. Interactive adaptations may use click, scroll, pointer, or raycast controls, with keyboard/touch alternatives where applicable; live input must not drive video export. Optional patterns such as impact-triggered growth, orb deformation, chapter transitions, or camera orbit/dolly require matching geometry and narrative purpose. Do not substitute ambient drift for their defining action.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, narration, effects, ambience, vocals, or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied choices, keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping, and synchronize and inspect the final mix.
assetRequirements: Create models, materials, lights, and cameras with Blender/bpy; bake simulations for frame rendering. Optional glTF assets need authorized licenses and inspected nodes, pivots, scale, and materials. Screens require aligned, composition-synchronized video textures. Prepare real depth geometry or sufficient turntable views for viewpoint changes; load and preload fonts and media.
combinations: Kinetic 2D titles over renders keep copy crisp; synchronize their direction and easing with camera motion and keep type out of 3D geometry. 2D leader-line callouts can explain features; attach them to exported anchors and show them when the object rests. These are suggested hybrids, not requirements.
productionApproach: Select renderer and motion method from the visual goal and action: Blender/Cycles or EEVEE for authored 3D, with optional browser rendering for suitable assets. Assign one owner per animated property. HyperFrames is the composition, timing, sync, validation, and export default; Remotion is allowed only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, with reason recorded. Keep visual and motion work in their own layers, expose deterministic time or baked assets, and inspect rendered frames and playback.
